speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, I think it is important that I make this Statement, so that I can highlight what these contradictions are and give the Member concerned an opportunity to state his position clearly for the record, as this relates to an important issue.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My understanding from Mr Faisal Manap is that there was no arrangement to meet him specifically." So, Mr Singh's position was that Mr Deros had "gate-crashed" Mr Faisal's meeting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Workers' Party (WP) Malay/Muslim candidates attended this meeting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Singh also referred to an earlier statement he had made during the elections in the following terms: "There was no indication that this individual", meaning Mr Deros, "would be joining in the meeting".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He also said that this could be verified with Mr Faisal Manap himself.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Thus, Mr Deros says that Mr Singh's claim that Mr Deros had gate-crashed was "irresponsible".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He does not refer to Mr Singh by name, but refers to the point made that he had gate-crashed.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Deros has been publicly asked whether he had really been invited and if so, whether he had been invited by Mr Faisal Manap or someone else.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Deros has replied publicly that the names of the asatizahs who would be present at the meeting had been sent to Mr Faisal Manap before the meeting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Thus, Mr Deros has suggested that Mr Faisal, at least, would have known that Mr Deros would be attending the meeting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And so, may I seek some clarifications from Mr Singh?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, can he confirm it is also Mr Faisal's position that Mr Deros had "gate-crashed" the meeting?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Faisal would know his answers to Mr Singh would be for this House.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, has Mr Singh confirmed with Mr Faisal whether the names of the asatizahs attending the meeting was sent in advance to Mr Faisal?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the names of the asatizahs attending the meeting were not sent in advance, was Mr Faisal nevertheless aware that Mr Deros would be attending the meeting?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I will now move onto my next set of clarifications.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (b) Mr Faisal said publicly then that he backed the movement.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (c) Members of the Wear White team gathered for the first Terawih, which are evening prayers during Ramadan at Masjid Ar-Raudhah on 28 June 2014.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members of the public were invited to join in the prayers.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (d) It is also a matter of public record that Mr Faisal attended that event.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just for a matter of record, before the Ministerial Statement was made, I communicated with Speaker, to inform Speaker last night that I would seek to make a clarification on certain representations that I had made in the House which were incorrect and they had to be clarified for the record.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, just to be clear, I am responding through Standing Order No 25.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Standing Order No 25 requires me to send to the Speaker in advance what I am going to share with this House and I will stick to that, notwithstanding Leader's questions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But apart from one point, I think all the questions that she has asked in her Ministerial Statement will be dealt with in the Personal Explanation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I had stated, referencing my remarks at the WP's 26 April 2025 doorstop interview with the press that, I quote: "There was no indication that this individual would be joining in the meeting." By this individual I am referring to a Singaporean Citizen one Noor Deros.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On 21 October 2025, about a week after the Ministerial Statement, Mr Faisal Manap shared with me a WhatsApp message that he received on his mobile device at the material time.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I was not aware of this detail in April this year, nor was I aware of it last month during the exchange on the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In view of this, I asked Mr Faisal to provide context for the meeting where Mr Noor Deros was present in view of the Ministerial Statement and the Parliamentary consensus that race and religion should not be used for political gain.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I said in Parliament last month that the meeting in question was arranged by an ustaz who was known to Mr Faisal.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The meeting took place on 20 April this year.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I said, quoting Mr Deros's Facebook post of 3 May 2025 that he attended the meeting at the invitation of an ustaz who was delegated by Mr Faisal.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This is correct and consistent with the facts of the meeting.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Mr Faisal shared that after GE 2011, he had approached an ustaz who was involved in inter-faith discourse to seek guidance on how he, being a minority Malay/Muslim MP could perform his role in a way that would best fit Singapore's multi-religious and multi-cultural society.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: He found the guidance helpful and meaningful, and hence, prior to GE 2015, he arranged for a similar session with an ustaz for himself and the WP Malay candidates to seek guidance and advice.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Mr Faisal confirms that the motives behind the meeting prior to GE 2025, which was attended by Mr Noor Deros, were the same.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On 12 April 2025, before Parliament was dissolved and Nomination Day announced, the ustaz who invited Mr Noor Deros, reached out to Mr Faisal informing him that he was planning to engage with the group of his asatizah friends to meet Mr Faisal to exchange ideas and thoughts.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In response, Mr Faisal said that he planned to engage with the ustaz for a sharing session with other WP Malay candidates in the lead-up to GE 2025.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This has been reconfirmed to me by Mr Faisal and the WP Malay/Muslim candidates who were present at the meeting.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: During the Parliamentary exchange last month, I also said that Mr Noor Deros gate-crashed the meeting.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe that deals with the Personal Explanation that I am obliged to share with Speaker, as per the Standing Orders.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There was an additional question from the Leader that pertained to Mr Noor Deros being a nobody.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I have confirmed in the statement that the WP Malay/Muslim candidates confirmed that there were no promises or undertakings made.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: They also confirmed that they did not know who Mr Noor Deros was.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Mr Faisal, as the Leader of the House shares, must have been known to Mr Deros because he was present at this Wear White event.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, Mr Faisal Manap would have known of who Mr Noor Deros was.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I hope that clarifies the query that the Leader put.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And if I have not addressed any point, I would be grateful if Leader could repeat the question.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am grateful to Mr Singh for his clarification.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, on the second point, the point that Mr Deros was a "nobody" and really, nobody knows of him.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If I understand Mr Singh's explanation correctly, you said Mr Faisal Manap would have known Mr Deros?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I just want to make sure that I get that correct.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In other words, is it correct to say that Mr Faisal Manap knew who Mr Deros was or knew Mr Deros before that meeting in April?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In other words, the statement that Mr Deros is somebody who really nobody knows, is not accurate.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On my personal basis, I did not know who Mr Noor Deros was as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, in that context, that is what I mean when I say Mr Noor Deros is a nobody.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think Mr Singh says he himself does not know Mr Deros – that, we are clear.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think Mr Singh has also said that the other Malay/Muslim candidates, other than Mr Faisal, did not know Mr Deros – that one, we are clear.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The thing that Mr Singh has just said is that Mr Faisal Manap would have "known of" Mr Deros.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is a distinction between saying Mr Faisal Manap would have "known of" him; for example, I know of many other world leaders, but I do not know them personally.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is a distinction between saying Mr Faisal Manap would have "known of" Mr Deros and Mr Faisal Manap would have "known" Mr Deros.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, what I am trying to understand here is whether Mr Faisal Manap just would have "known of", which means you hear of this person, but you do not know them, or whether he knew him.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Did he know of him or did know of him as an individual?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think the Leader shared a particular occasion where both of them were at a common platform.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: To the extent of how much Mr Faisal Manap knew of Mr Deros, I am not in a position to relay any information in that regard.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I have seen pictures to that effect of both Mr Faisal and Mr Noor Deros being at that event that the Leader mentioned.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I cannot stand here and suggest or even imply the extent of how well they knew each other.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, now I move to the first point on this question of gate-crashing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I was not sure that I quite understood Mr Singh's clarification here.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In light of the clarification, because I think it is important to go back to the original statement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It would not be right to leave that impression on the record.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Hence, my decision to make a Personal Explanation, on my own volition, today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The position, of course, is not known to me that he was — based on what I had said in April was based on the knowledge I had in April and the knowledge that I had in October.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, it is knowledge that I received after the fact.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I have made certain statements in Parliament about it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I come to Parliament and I correct the impression that I have left with Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is quite clear that – Mr Singh has clarified it now – because he says the knowledge that Mr Deros was included in the group was given to him on 21 October.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What I want to know is, because Mr Singh had said during the elections that Mr Deros had gate-crashed the meeting, and Mr Singh had said the same thing on 14 October 2025; because on 14 October what Mr Singh said was, "I mentioned quite clearly during the elections that he had gate-crashed the meeting", I just want to know during the elections in April and on 14 October, on what basis does Mr Singh say that Mr Deros had gate-crashed the meeting?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The basis is the fact that Mr Deros was not invited by Mr Faisal.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, my impression based on what had transpired at the elections and also, in the course of the Ministerial Statement was, there was no WP member who specifically sought out Mr Noor Deros.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That also has been stated in my Personal Explanation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will not belabour the point, but I just want to wrap it up by saying this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is actually a difference between saying that Mr Deros was not specifically sought out.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Not specifically sought out is one thing, but "gate-crashed" really implies – not even supposed to be there, not invited.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And what the facts do show now is that he was invited by the ustaz, and that the ustaz had informed Mr Faisal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think, in short, had this been known in April during the elections and made known to the voters, I think it might have put a different colour on the circumstances then.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And also, it is an odd word to use – "gate-crashed" – if you have not actually verified that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am not sure that the statement that "gate-crashed" means "did not seek out", actually makes sense.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I can understand where the Leader is coming from.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I do not believe there are any other outstanding matters.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Leader can correct me if that is not the case.
